_about: The holiness hub (plan 7.6f), the fourth after love, righteousness and peace, built to the same level. Holiness is one family in the Hebrew and Greek -- קָדוֹשׁ and ἅγιος (holy), קֹדֶשׁ (holiness, the holy place, holy things), קָדַשׁ and ἁγιάζω (to make holy), מִקְדָּשׁ (sanctuary), ἁγιασμός, ἁγιότης, ἁγιωσύνη (holiness, sanctification) -- and the English renders it holy, sanctify, consecrate, dedicate, sacred, sanctuary and saints. The committee (2026-10-09) flagged it medium: ἅγιος is mostly the Spirit's title (89 of 222 verses), and how the saints come to be holy is argued by Wesleyan, Pentecostal, Reformed, Catholic and Orthodox readers. So: the rows are split by who or what is called holy; 'the Holy Spirit' and 'the Holy One' are by hand; 'saints' is kept as the Berean writes it; the contested point is set out as rows side by side. The Hebrew nouns sit under the noun form and the Greek adjective under the adjective form -- the grammar, not a different sense; the hub is the whole family. Rows as in love.json and righteousness.json; match 'all'. Built by tools/concepts/hub_build.py.

titles.adjective: Who and what is called holy
titles.noun: Holiness, the holy place and holy things

_words_why: The family in both testaments: קָדוֹשׁ and Aramaic קַדִּישׁ with ἅγιος (the Greek Old Testament renders qodesh and qadosh by ἅγιος, and the LXX of Daniel the Aramaic), קֹדֶשׁ, מִקְדָּשׁ, קָדַשׁ with ἁγιάζω, and the Greek nouns ἁγιασμός, ἁγιότης, ἁγιωσύνη. Left out as different words: קֶדֶשׁ and קָדֵשׁ the places Kedesh and Kadesh, קָדֵשׁ the temple prostitute (the same letters, another word), and ὅσιος, ὁσιότης, ἁγνός, ἱερός, דְּבִיר -- the English also says 'holy', 'sacred' or 'sanctuary' for them; they are named apart below.
_sense_why: Empty: every use of these words is in the concept's range -- holy, sanctuary, sacred donations, dedicated gifts, saints, consecrate, set apart -- the Berean's glosses for one word. Nothing is dropped by the English; the rows divide the uses by what is holy.

others._why: Words the English renders holy, sacred, sanctify, sanctuary or saint that are not this family: ὅσιος 'holy One' (Acts 2:27, 13:35; Rev 16:5), ὁσιότης 'holiness' (Luke 1:75, Eph 4:24), דְּבִיר 'sanctuary' (the inner room of Solomon's temple), נֵזֶר 'consecration' (the Nazirite's hair), ἱερός 'sacred' Scriptures. Named apart with their verses; the reader is never handed one as the other. h4993 is a gloss stray; h4676 מַצֵּבָה is a pagan 'sacred pillar' and is no help to a reader of holiness. NOT FOUND HERE: חָסִיד (h2623), the faithful or loyal ones, which the Berean prints 'saints' in 16 of its 32 verses (Ps 31:23, 37:28, 97:10, 116:15, 145:10, 149:5 and others); this section matches MACULA's own gloss ('faithful'), not the Berean's English, so it cannot list them.
others.title: Other words translated “holy”, “saints”, “sacred”, “sanctuary”

Hos.12.1.why: the Hebrew's Hos 12:1 ('faithful to the Holy One') is printed in the Berean's 11:12; its 12:1 is the verse about Ephraim and the wind

1Sam.21.5.why: the lexicon numbers the Hebrew verses 21:5-7 where the Berean has 21:4-6: 'there is some consecrated bread' is the Berean's 21:4

1Sam.21.6.why: as 1Sam 21:5 above: the Hebrew's 21:6 ('the bodies of the young men are holy') is the Berean's 21:5

1Sam.21.7.why: as 1Sam 21:5 above: the Hebrew's 21:7 ('the priest gave him the holy bread') is the Berean's 21:6; the Berean's 21:7 is Doeg

rows.label: Be holy, because I am holy
rows._why: by hand: the verses where the LORD says it of Himself (Leviticus) and where Peter writes it as quoted; Lev 20:7 says 'be holy, because I am the LORD your God' and stands under 'A holy people'

rows.label: “The LORD our God is holy”, “Holy Father”, “Holy is His name”
rows._why: by hand, as the divine persons are: verses where the text itself says the LORD, God, the Father, or the One whose name is Holy (Isa 57:15; Luke 1:49 'the Mighty One ... Holy is His name') is holy. Ps 22:3 and 99:3 speak to Him ('You are holy', 'He is holy') in psalms that name Him. 'Lord, holy and true' (Rev 6:10) and 'the One who is holy and true' (Rev 3:7) say only the title and stand in the row after next

rows.label: The LORD, “the Holy One of Israel”
rows.note: The text also says “the Holy One of Jacob” (Isa 29:23), “the Holy One in Israel” (Ezek 39:7), “my Holy One” (Hab 1:12) and “the Holy One among you” (Hos 11:9); in each the LORD or God is named in the verse.
rows._why: by hand: every verse where the title stands with the LORD or God named in it. Isaiah's thirty uses are the bulk

rows.label: “The Holy One”, “holy and true”: the title without a name
rows.note: The verse gives the title and no name. Readers take the Old Testament verses of the LORD; of 1 John 2:20, Rev 3:7 and Rev 6:10 some readers take the Father and some Christ, and the page does not choose.
rows._why: the righteousness hub's 'He is righteous' row, for the same reason: the text says only the title. Hos 11:12 is the Berean's verse for the Hebrew's 12:1 (see moves)

rows.label: Jesus called holy
rows._why: by hand, as the divine persons are: verses where the text itself names Jesus holy -- 'Your holy servant Jesus' (Acts 4:27, 4:30), 'Jesus of Nazareth ... the Holy One of God' (Mark 1:24, Luke 4:34, said by an unclean spirit), 'You are the Holy One of God' (John 6:69, said to Jesus), 'the Holy and Righteous One' (Acts 3:14, of Jesus named in 3:13), the Holy One to be born (Luke 1:35, to Mary, who is told in 1:31 to name Him Jesus). Acts 2:27 and 13:35 'Your Holy One' are the different word ὅσιος and stand with the other words, not here

rows.label: “The Holy Spirit”
rows.note: “Holy” is the title the text gives the Spirit in these verses; they are listed together so they are not read as verses about holiness as a quality. Where the noun is used instead -- “the spirit of Your holiness”, “the Spirit of holiness” -- see the noun section below.
rows._why: by hand: the committee (2026-10-09) flagged that ἅγιος is mostly the Spirit's title and 'misleads' as holiness. 89 Greek verses where ἅγιος stands beside πνεῦμα (plus Eph 1:13, where the adjective follows the noun 'of promise'). Rom 15:19 is left out: the original has ἅγιος there (the Berean's 'the Spirit of God' follows another manuscript line) and a row labelled 'Holy Spirit' would show a verse without the words

rows.label: Holy angels, “holy ones”, “the saints of the Most High”
rows.note: Where the text says “holy ones” or “saints” without saying who, the page does not choose between heavenly beings and the LORD's people; readers part on Daniel 7 and on 1 Thessalonians 3:13 above all.
rows._why: 'holy angels' are named as angels; the rest say 'holy ones' and the verse alone does not settle who. Dan 4:13, 4:17, 4:23 are the Aramaic 'a watcher, a holy one'; Dan 7 the Aramaic 'saints of the Most High'

rows.label: A holy people, a holy nation
rows._why: by hand: where a people is called holy by the adjective. Num 16:3 is Korah's claim, kept as the text's own words. The Hebrew noun's 'My holy people' is the noun section's

rows.label: Priests, Levites and the Nazirite, holy to the LORD
A holy man, holy prophets and apostles, holy women
Called to be saints, called and chosen to be holy
rows.note: Where Christian traditions part on how the saints come to be holy -- in Christ at once, by growth over a life, or both -- the page sets the text's verses side by side (these, and the rows on “sanctified” and “sanctification”) and takes no side.
rows._why: Wesleyan, Pentecostal, Reformed, Catholic and Orthodox readers argue how saints come to be holy (committee, 2026-10-09). The labels are the text's own words ('called to be saints', 'chose us ... to be holy', 'present you holy')

rows.label: Letters to the saints: greetings to and from them; serving, loving and praying for them
rows._why: 'saints' kept as the Berean writes it for ἅγιοι, 'holy ones' (committee: 'keep saints phrases as written')

rows.label: The saints in Acts and Revelation: harmed, killed, praying, enduring
A holy place, holy ground, the holy city, the holy mountain, the holy temple
rows._why: the adjective for a place: Hebrew קָדוֹשׁ 'in a holy place', Greek ἅγιος 'the holy city' and τὰ ἅγια ('the Holy Place'; Heb 8:2, 9:12, 9:24, 9:25, 10:19, 13:11 are 'holy places' in the Berean, the sanctuary). The Hebrew noun קֹדֶשׁ ('holy mountain', 'holy place', 'holy ground') is under the noun form below; this is the grammar, not a different sense

rows.label: Every other use
“Majestic in holiness”, “the splendor of holiness”, “sworn by My holiness”, the Way of Holiness
rows._why: by hand: the nine verses where the Berean prints the abstract 'holiness' for קֹדֶשׁ, all of the LORD's but the Way of Holiness

rows.label: Holiness that is God's: “share in His holiness”, “sanctified by the Spirit”, Christ “our holiness”
rows.note: Set beside the next row, as the letters have them. Where Christian traditions part on whether holiness is given in Christ at once, grown into over a life, or both, the page takes no side.
rows._why: ἁγιασμός, ἁγιότης (Greek nouns); picked by what each verse ties holiness to -- God, the Spirit, Christ -- and not by the Berean's rendering 'sanctification' or 'holiness', which differ for the same word

rows.label: Holiness as the aim and fruit of the life: “pursue holiness”, “perfecting holiness”, “leads to holiness”, “called ... to holiness”
rows.note: Set beside the row above; a verse that fits both would stand in both. The page takes no side on how the two are held together.
rows._why: the other side of the contested point, from the same Greek nouns; ἁγιωσύνη (2 Cor 7:1, 1 Thess 3:13) is 'holiness' in the Berean as ἁγιασμός is

rows.label: “Your Holy Spirit”, “the Spirit of holiness”
rows.note: The Hebrew says “the spirit of Your holiness”; Romans 1:4 says “the Spirit of holiness”. The 89 verses that say “the Holy Spirit” with the adjective are in the first section.
rows._why: by hand: the noun, not the adjective, is used; the builder files them by part of speech

rows.label: The Most Holy Place, the most holy things
rows._why: the Hebrew's superlative is the word repeated ('holy of holies'): קֹדֶשׁ beside קֹדֶשׁ, by the phrase, not by the Berean's rendering

rows.label: The sanctuary, the holy place, holy ground
rows._why: מִקְדָּשׁ (all 72 verses) and the Berean's 'sanctuary', 'Holy Place' and 'holy ground' for קֹדֶשׁ, as an explicit list: the lexicon's occurrence list leaves out Lev 10:4, 16:17 and Ezek 44:7, which only a pick can place. The 'sanctuary shekel' verses, a measure, are left to the last row

rows.label: The holy mountain, the holy city, the holy temple, the holy dwelling

not_verses.Dan.9.26: 'the city and the sanctuary' are two things destroyed; the word is the sanctuary, not 'holy city'

rows.label: “My holy name”, “His holy name”
rows._why: by the phrase (the name beside קֹדֶשׁ); 1 Chr 16:35 and Ps 106:47 are among the nine verses the lexicon's occurrence list leaves out, so the row is a list

rows.label: Holy days: the Sabbath, the sacred assemblies, the Jubilee
Holy things: garments, anointing oil, offerings, dedicated gifts, the holy portion
rows._why: the Berean's 'holy things', 'sacred donations', 'dedicated gifts', 'votive gifts', 'holy garments', 'sacred anointing oil' and 'holy portion' for קֹדֶשׁ, as a list: first found by the garment, oil and offering words beside it (בֶּגֶד, מִשְׁחָה, שֶׁמֶן, נֵזֶר, תְּרוּמָה, כְּלִי, אוֹצָר), then added by the Berean's own renderings

rows.label: “HOLY TO THE LORD”
rows._why: by the phrase in the Berean: 'holy to the LORD', 'holy to you', 'set apart to the LORD'. The plate on the high priest's forehead, and what Zechariah says will carry it

rows.label: “My holy people”, “the Holy People”, “the holy seed”
rows._why: the Hebrew noun used of a people; the adjective's holy people are in the first section

rows.label: What is the LORD's is called holy: His arm, covenant, word, throne, heaven, land, way
“Between the holy and the common”
rows._why: Ezek 42:20 and 44:23 carry the word in the Hebrew, but the lexicon's occurrence list does not hold them, so they are picked

rows.label: Profaned, defiled: the sanctuary, the holy name, the holy things, the Sabbath

not_verses.Lev.10.10: 'unclean', the adjective, beside 'the common'; nothing is profaned
not_verses.Isa.35.8: 'the unclean will not travel it': the adjective, not an act of defiling
not_verses.Isa.52.1: 'the unclean': the adjective, not an act of defiling

rows.label: Every other use
God sanctifies: “I am the LORD who sanctifies you”
rows._why: by hand, as the divine persons are: the verses where the LORD, God or the Father is the one who sanctifies, in the verse or in the speech it belongs to (Num 3:13, 8:17, 1 Kgs 9:3, 7, 2 Chr 7:16, 20 are His own first-person words)

rows.label: Jesus sanctifies: “for them I sanctify Myself”, “by His own blood”
rows._why: by hand: Heb 2:11 and 13:12 name Jesus; John 17:19 is His prayer ('Myself'); Eph 5:26 is Christ, named in 5:25, whom the verb's frame gives as the subject

rows.label: Hallow the name, regard the LORD as holy, “sanctify Christ as Lord”; “I will show Myself holy”
Consecrate yourselves; consecrate the priests, the altar, the tabernacle, the house
Set apart to the LORD: the firstborn, a house, a field, gifts
Keep the Sabbath day holy
Whatever touches it becomes holy
rows.note: In Haggai the priests are asked whether consecrated meat makes other food holy by touching it, and they answer no (2:12).

rows.label: Sanctified by: the truth, the word, faith, the blood, the sacrifice, the Spirit, a believing spouse
rows._why: by what each verse names as the means, in its own words; the page does not rank them. 1 Cor 7:14 ('sanctified through his believing wife') is here because the verse says 'sanctified' and names a means; the label says so; readers part on what it shows of the children (it is also a point in the baptism debates) and the page says nothing of that

rows.label: “Having been sanctified”, “you were sanctified”
rows.note: Set beside the next row, as Hebrews 10:10 and 10:14 stand together. Where Christian traditions part on whether sanctification is finished at once, a lifelong process, a second crisis, or all of these, the page takes no side.
rows._why: side by side, committee 2026-10-09 (Wesleyan, Pentecostal, Reformed, Catholic, Orthodox): the Greek perfect and aorist passives, as the Berean renders them 'having been sanctified' and 'you were sanctified'

rows.label: “Being sanctified”, “sanctify you completely”, “let the holy continue to be holy”
rows.note: Set beside the row above. A verse that fits both stands in both; the page takes no side.
rows._why: the other side: the present participle (Heb 10:14), the prayer for it to be done (1 Thess 5:23, John 17:17, 19) and the command to continue (Rev 22:11)

rows.label: “Prepare for battle”, “prepare for war”, “declare war”
rows.note: The Hebrew verb is the one rendered consecrate and sanctify elsewhere: literally to sanctify a war. The Berean prints “prepare” and “declare”.
rows._why: the original arbitrates: the word is qadash; the Berean does not print 'consecrate'

rows.label: Every other use
